column1: # A light strip that can become a Matter device without being opened up again.
# THIS IS THE ONE THING THAT CANNOT BE CHANGED OVER THE AIR. An update writes the other app slot and
# flips otadata; it cannot move the slots themselves. So a unit that ships on a table too small for
# Matter can never become a Matter device
column2: and the household would have to send it back. The bridge

column1: # puck already learned the shallow version of this -- it shipped once on huge_app.csv
# app slot
column2: and so could never be updated remotely at all (docs/puck-updates.md).

column1: # Sized for 8 MB
column2: which is the floor for the module we would actually buy; it loads unchanged on a

column1: # 16 MB part and simply leaves the top unused. The current firmware is about 940 KB and a Matter
# application on this silicon runs 1.5-2 MB
column2: so 3.75 MB a slot is room for Matter plus years of it

column1: # getting fatter -- which is the point
column2: because this number is the one we only get to pick once.

column1: # Two partitions here are for a Matter device that is CERTIFIED rather than one running on a test
# vendor id
column2: and they are laid down now for the same reason:

column1: #   esp_secure_cert  the per-unit Device Attestation Certificate and its key
#                    (Espressif provision this as a service; every shipped unit needs its own)
#   fctry            the factory data esp-matter reads its vendor id
#                    from
column2: kept apart from nvs so a factory reset cannot take the identity with it

column1: #   coredump         where a crash writes itself down. A strip in somebody's living room that reboots
#                    once a week is otherwise undiagnosable: nobody is watching a serial port when it
#                    happens
column2: and the only evidence is gone by the time anybody asks. The first boot

column1: #                    said "No core dump partition found" and that was the cheapest possible moment to
#                    notice
column2: because this table is the one thing an update cannot change.
